Which key is that?

This page reads the keys of your Logitech Harmony remote while it is connected to this computer with its USB cable. It can learn which number your remote uses for each key, so that you can send us the key map of a model we do not have, and it can test whether every key on your remote still works.

What it does, and what it does not

  • It only reads. It asks the remote two things: its version, which says which model it is, and two bytes of its working memory, where the remote keeps the key being held and the last key pressed. It never writes to the remote and never changes its setup.
  • Nothing leaves your browser. There is no server behind this page and nothing is sent anywhere. The key map it writes for you is text you copy yourself, and it holds the model, the keys and their numbers, and nothing that identifies your remote.
  • It works with the Harmony 880, 885, 880 Pro and 720, in Chrome or Edge on a computer. Other remotes are not offered in the list, and a remote that is not running normally, such as one held in its recovery mode, is let go without its keys being read.

Plug your remote in, then press Connect.

Do not press GLOW (the light key). On these remotes it switches the screen off and ends the connection. If it happens: unplug the cable, plug it back in, and press Reconnect.

The models this page reads

    Step 2: Learn the key map

    Press each key twice. The second press confirms the first; if they differ, both are dropped and the key is asked again.

    This key did not reach the page in step 1. Press it to try again; if your remote reacts to it and nothing happens here, it works but the page does not see it.

    • blue with a heavy edge: the key to press now
    • blue with rings and a dashed edge: pressed once, press it again to confirm
    • orange with dots: learned
    • grey with lines: skipped, my remote has no such key
    • white with crosses: works, but the page does not see it

    Step 1: Test all keys

    Press every key once, except Glow.

    Do not press Glow, the light key: it ends the connection. This step shows which keys reach this page. Each key you press stays marked, so a key that never gets marked is one the page did not see. Then go on to step 2.

    • orange with dots: this key answered
    • orange with white bands: one of these keys answered, and which of them is not known yet
    • black and yellow bands: do not press this key

    Other keys that answered, by number

      None so far.

      Step 3: Check the key map

      Press the keys again, except Glow.

      Each key you press lights by the key map you just made. If the key that lights is not the one you pressed, that key was learned wrong: go back to step 2, undo, and learn it again.

      • orange with dots: lit by the key map
      • orange with white bands: one of these keys, and which of them is not known yet
      • black and yellow bands: do not press this key

        Your key map

        It grows as you go. When you are done, copy it and send it to us as a new issue on the harmony-explorations repository on GitHub. It holds the model, the keys and their numbers, and nothing that identifies your remote.
